subject: Renewal: transition to auto-renew with progressive capacity ladder
messages:
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@omaptech.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: billing@omaptech.com
Date: 2026-10-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming Renewal — options and term structuring

Marcus,

Hope youre well. Our renewal for Redwood services comes up at the end of October and procurement wants to understand the options we have for term structure and capacity growth over a multi-year commitment. A few things were evaluating:

- Ability to co-term with our other cloud contracts in Q1 so billing lines align
- An auto-renew mechanism (we prefer auto-renew with explicit opt-out)
- A predictable ramp: year 1 lower committed baseline with step-ups in years 2 and 3
- Pricing protection / fixed unit price vs an annual escalator

Can you send the available templates or a proposal with a couple of scenarios? Also copy legal/procurement on any standard SOW or payment schedule.

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Head of Data Platforms
OmapTech

[Attachment: procurement_vendors_list.csv (CSV)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@omaptech.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: Options for multi-year progressive capacity ladder

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear ask. Ive put together three proposals attached so you can choose the posture that best fits OmapTechs growth forecast. High level:

1) Locked-commit (3yr) — fixed units per year, deepest discount (best if you want price stability).
2) Progressive capacity ladder (recommended) — lower year-1 commit, pre-agreed step-ups in years 2 and 3, annual unit price protection on agreed increments, includes a burst buffer for spikes.
3) Elastic baseline + overage — smaller committed baseline with lower unit price on pre-committed capacity and consumption-based billing for overage.

Attached: RDW_Proposal_Progressive_Ladder_2026.pdf (proposal), SOW-draft.docx (editable SOW).

A few notes on auto-renew: we can mark the contract to auto-renew annually with a 60-day opt-out window. For multi-year deals we typically require a minimum renewal term cadence (e.g., 12-month renewals inside a 36-month commit) to preserve discounts.

Next steps I suggest:
- You and procurement pick scenario 1/2/3 (or suggest a hybrid)
- Ill loop in Sales Ops to produce an invoice schedule and run the co-term calculation across your other vendor renewals
- Legal can sync on the SOW redlines after you indicate the scenario

If helpful, we can do a 30-min call tomorrow to walk the ladder math.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

[Attachments: RDW_Proposal_Progressive_Ladder_2026.pdf (PDF); SOW-draft.docx (DOCX)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-12T08:10:00-07:00
Subject: FW: OmapTech renewal — pricing posture & escalation ask

FYI — OmapTech is leaning toward a progressive ladder (scenario 2). Key asks from procurement: co-term with other Q1 contracts, auto-renew default with explicit opt-out, and a year-1 light commit + step-ups in years 2 and 3.

Questions for Ops/CS:
- Karthik: can you prepare a tiered invoice schedule that shows quarterly billing, proration if they opt to co-term earlier, and the frontloaded credit option (6 months of credits up-front to help onboarding)?
- Monica: once we have the schedule Id like you to confirm onboarding milestones tied to a 10% ramp credit release (to reduce churn risk).

We may need a small one-time concession (first-quarter credit) to close this as theyre evaluating a competing provider for a portion of their workload. If you see any administrative hurdles with an auto-renew clause for a 36-month agreement, flag them here.

Thanks,
Marcus

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: OmapTech renewal — pricing posture & escalation ask

Marcus — attaching a suggested payment schedule and a short example of how the ladder would amortize across the 36 months. Highlights:
- Year 1 commit: 40% of peak baseline; Year 2 commit: 70%; Year 3 commit: 100%
- Unit price on committed units is locked for the 36-month period for the pre-agreed increments; overage priced at on-demand rate with a 10% discount for sustained overage >3 months
- Suggested frontloaded credit: 3 months of equivalent committed usage applied to onboarding invoices (one-time credit).
- Co-term handling: allow proration and conversion of unused credits if customer co-terms earlier; requires an addendum.

Ive attached payment_schedule.xlsx — if this looks good I can generate a DocuSign envelope with the SOW and payment schedule attached.

[Karthik Iyer
Sales Operations, Redwood Inference]

Subject: Renewal agreement in principle — next steps and DocuSign

Hi Lena — appreciate the alignment this week. Per our conversations, heres what we have agreed in principle:

- Structure: Progressive capacity ladder (3-year) — Year1: 40%, Year2: 70%, Year3: 100% of projected peak baseline
- Auto-renew: annual auto-renew with 60-day opt-out window; multi-year discounts preserved on pre-agreed increments
- Credits: one-time onboarding credit equal to 3 months of Year1 committed usage
- Co-term: addendum to convert/prorate unused credits if co-term occurs within the 36-month period

Ive asked Sales Ops to prepare the DocuSign envelope. Youll receive: the SOW (editable), the payment schedule, and the proposal PDF. Please review and advise any legal redlines; we can incorporate through an addendum.
